problem: SG049's positive-vs-zero label mapping treats significant negative trend as rejection of positive drift; cannot identify genuine negative trend.

method.generator: Nine prior synthetic noise scenarios, exact same noise parameters, but programmed slope sign in {-1,0,+1}. Weak drift magnitude .0027; all others .005. Both policies see identical 240-point continuation and same HAC(3) slope from ten-point bin medians.
method.interval: Full240 OLS/HAC lag3, interval slope ± 2.291027529910169*SE, fixed from SG049.
method.SG049_projection: CI lower>0 => positive, CI upper<0 => zero (reject positive hypothesis), CI inside ±.0032 => zero, otherwise unresolved. A deliberately positive-only projection; does not claim full SG049 boundary challenge replication.
method.SG050: CI lower>0 => positive, upper<0 => negative, CI wholly inside ±.0032 => zero, else unresolved.
method.cost: 14.4 sample cost for 240 observations; incorrect nonzero directional claim 150; reporting zero when true nonzero 90; unresolved 18. Same loss function across policies.
method.nonleakage: Decisions use only numeric continuation observations and a precommitted rule; generator true sign is used only to score.

pilot.disclosure: Pilot inspected. SG050 improves sensitivity to genuine negative trend but raises false directional claims from 3 to 9. No retuning after pilot.

phase_progress: Count 1/12 (8.3%) only after source, freeze, complete holdout, GitHub record and index verified
limitations: Synthetic scenarios previously known; fresh seeds and genuine negative ground truth but no new independent real-world validation.
One-sided and two-sided statistical semantics differ; SG049 projection lacks its boundary-warning challenge.
False direction penalty selected as synthetic decision model, not empirical impact.
The old positive-only formulation was not designed to classify negative drift; ranking both on ternary labels is a changed task.
